sections.heading: Opening

Per the file, these accts are populated at known (per the file) addresses published along with the acct layouts in the solana-program crate, and outlined below. Per the file, there are two ways (per the file) for a program to access a sysvar.

Per the file, the first is to (per the file) query the sysvar at (per the file) runtime via the sysvar's get() function: The following sysvars support get: (per the file) Clock EpochSchedule Fees Rent EpochRewards (per the file) The second is to pass (per the file) the sysvar to the program as an acct by including its address as (per the file) one of the accts in the Instruction and then (per the file) deserializing the data during execution. Per the file, access to sysvars accts is always _readonly_.

Per the file, the first method is more efficient and fails to require that the sysvar acct be passed to the (per the file) program, or specified in (per the file) the Instruction the program is processing. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

paragraphs: Per the file, the Clock sysvar contains (per the file) data on cluster time, (per the file) including the current slot, (per the file) epoch, and estimated wall-clock Unix timestamp. Per the file, in the first slot (per the file) of an epoch, this (per the file) timestamp is identical to (per the file) the unix_timestamp (below). epoch: (per the file) the current epoch leader_schedule_epoch: the (per the file) most recent epoch for which the leader (per the file) schedule has already been generated unix_timestamp: the (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) Unix timestamp of this slot. Per the file, each slot has an (per the file) estimated duration based on Proof of History.

Per the file, but in reality, slots (per the file) may elapse faster and (per the file) slower than this estimate. Per the file, as a result, the (per the file) Unix timestamp of a (per the file) slot is generated based (per the file) on oracle input from voting nodes. Per the file, this timestamp is calculated (per the file) as the stake-weighted median (per the file) of timestamp estimates provided by (per the file) votes, bounded by the expected (per the file) time elapsed since the start (per the file) of the epoch.

Per the file, more explicitly: for each (per the file) slot, the most recent (per the file) vote timestamp provided by each node is used to generate (per the file) a timestamp estimate for (per the file) the current slot (the (per the file) elapsed slots since the (per the file) vote timestamp are assumed (per the file) to be Bank::ns_per_slot). Per the file, each timestamp estimate is (per the file) associated with the stake (per the file) delegated to that vote acct to create a distribution (per the file) of timestamps by stake.

Per the file, the median timestamp is (per the file) used as the unix_timestamp, (per the file) unless the elapsed time since (per the file) the epoch_start_timestamp has deviated from (per the file) the expected elapsed time by more than (per the file) 25%.
